raw: The driver of the coach changed the horses at a station that stood near a river ford. While stopped there, he also took on a new passenger—a man who was quiet in manner and who carried a leather case. Once the coach passed beyond a ridge, the road climbed upward through pine trees. During this stretch of the journey, the coach's guard kept his rifle resting across his knees. He held it that way until the lights of a mining town came into view, at which point the coach rolled into the town. The coach's arrival was an hour later than the time expected in the answer to the office's telegram—that is, a reply had been sent back to a telegram from the office stating when the coach was expected, and the coach came in one hour after that expected time.

There was a problem with reception: interference from a nearby power line created a hissing noise spread across the band. Nevertheless, a distant station eventually managed to come through. Its signal was strong enough that the two operators were able to hold a short conversation with each other. The topics of their exchange were antennas and the season, which was fading — that is, the time of year drawing toward its end. The contact came to a close when the rest of the household called for the lamp and for bed, bringing the operator's evening on the air to an end.
